newsitem.title: UK: Shell Rotterdam pipe cracked, gas oil short - trade.
newsitem.headline: Shell Rotterdam pipe cracked, gas oil short - trade.

text.p: The unexpected closure of an oil product import pipeline at Shell's Pernis refinery in the Netherlands has forced the company to buy large amounts of gas oil on the Rotterdam market to cover its downstream requirements, traders said on Monday.

Shell bought around 30,000 tonnes of heating oil barges on Monday, driving premiums up $1.50 to $8.50 over Oct IPE futures, and was still looking for more supply on Monday evening, including low sulphur diesel fuel, they added.
"They are missing quality and quantity," a trader said.
The pipeline, used to carry gas oil and naphtha from the Europoort terminal to the 370,000 barrel-per-day refinery, was closed after a crack was discovered on a weld, traders said.

A Shell spokesman said the pipeline was due to be shut this week for maintenance anyway, but was closed early after the crack was discovered. He expected the pipeline to return to service "in a fortnight or so".
He said the closure had no impact on refinery operation.
Traders said a hydro-desulphurisation unit, used to remove sulphur from gas oil, was already in planned maintenance.
Traders estimated the company would have to buy about 15,000 tonnes of gas oil per day to feed its downstream network while the pipeline remained closed.
